Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

This is class number two.

Key details

  • I am Dr.
  • Sv. from Civil Engineering under Department of Science and Humanities.
  • under PS University.
  • In the very first class we discussed a few things regarding this subject, that is what is indicated here in this slide.
  • We came to know what is meant by mechanics, the different between statics and dynamics.
  • Then the definitions, few of the definitions of space, mass, time, particle, rigid body, elastic body, plastic body.
  • Then we define what is a force, what are the types of forces, what are the units of forces in S side.
  • What are Newton's laws?
  • And then we discussed about the characteristics of forces.
  • In between, I also discussed about the prerequisite for understanding these subjects.
  • That is mathematics, then physics, and of course.
  • English that was required.
  • This is class number two.
  • First of the foremost thing is similar triangles under geometry.
  • You all know what are similar triangles.
  • One side and two angles or two sides and one angle, if they are proportional to each other in these two triangles, then we call them as similar triangles.
  • If you take a triangle, any triangle, then.
  • If a side is the distance of the side is taken as capital A, the angle opposite to this side in the triangle is taken as small A.
  • Small b, the last side, if the distance is taken as capital C and the angle opposite to this side is taken as small a, then the sides of the triangle.
  • Will be proportional to the sine of the angle opposite to the other two angles or opposite to this side or angle between the other two sides.
  • So that means A by capital A divided by sine of small A, that is the angle made by the.
  • other two sides other than capital A is small.
  • What is law of cosine?
  • Again, we take a triangle, any general triangle.
  • If the sites are named as the distances of the sites are named as A, B, and C, and the angle opposite to side A is taken as small A.
  • Then we can say that the distance of the side A, capital A, A square is equal to.
  • B square plus C square minus 2 B C into cos of angles A.
  • So that means.
  • When you have a triangle, we can determine the any side of the triangle if we know two sides and one angle which is opposite to the side of the distance for which we have to calculate, then we can do it easily by using law of cosines.
  • Next comes what is complementary angle.
  • All of that complementary angles sum up to 90 degrees.
  • Supplementary angle is the sum of two angles will come to 180 degrees.
  • Corresponding angles will always be equal.

Example or application from the lecture

  • Then let's understand what is law of science.
  • Next, let us look at what is law of cosine.

Core explanation · 05:00–09:59

Alternate angles are also will have equal angles between them.

Key details

  • The vertically opposite angles also will be equal to each other.
  • And of course tripometry basics of trigonometry is required.
  • Then of course basics of integration is also required to certain extent.
  • Next comes this.
  • Few things that we need to understand.
  • That is first one is deformation.
  • What is deformation?
  • No, when you take a body and there is a force applied onto this body, the body's shape will change.
  • But the position of the body would not change.
  • Changes when you apply a force is called as deformation.
  • The position of the body does not change, only the shape of the body changes.
  • Will change whereas the position does not change.
  • The next one is displacement.
  • This change in the position of the object because of the application of the force is called as displacement.
  • The body is getting displaced from one point to another point because of application of the force.
  • What is defluction?
  • We have two poles and in between we have an electrical wire.
  • Over a period of time, because of its own weight, this wire would actually bent or it will take a shape of a bow okay when you have a bow inverted or kept it horizontal you can see that it will have a shape like the sector of a s curve okay or it will take the shape of a curve it's a sector of a circle okay.
  • Now that is because of the sulfate of the wire itself.
  • No, if you take any point on this wire, the.
  • Body has undone the shape change because it was horizontal, now it has changed to a curve one.
  • And again the position of that point would have changed, it would have come down.
  • So there is both deformation and displacement occurring simultaneously in an object, such changes is defined as deflection.
  • There could be a change in the position of the body, or the shape of the body can change, or there could be deflection.
  • Any of this or combination of this can occur.
  • In the last class also, I talked about coordinate system, whether it is three-dimensional or two-dimensional.

Example or application from the lecture

  • The best example is you take a sponge and when you apply force onto this, the shape of the sponge.
  • That's the best example for understanding what is deformation.
  • Now, you take a body, and when you apply a force onto body, for example, let me take this pen.

Core explanation · 10:00–14:59

But I also told you that we use the right hand first three fingers to take or to note the directions of the coordinate system.

Key details

  • Then the forefinger will be y-axis and the middle finger will be the z axis.
  • The three fingers that I am taking of my right hand is also mutually perpendicular to each other.
  • To each other.
  • But when I if I apply a force onto this, say I will take this as x-axis and this as y-axis, and I am applying a force onto this pen along the x-axis or only along the y-axis or only in the plane x y.
  • I'm not going to be applying the force normal to this XY or along the Z axis, then I can represent these forces only in these two planes, that is X and Y.
  • Forces onto this body will also occur in the same plane.
  • Then we can treat this as a two-dimensional force system.
  • Next, we will look at what is translatory motion.
  • I talked about displacement earlier when I told you that if there is a force applied on to a body, if the position of the body changes from one position to another position because of application of the force.
  • that without any change in the shape of the body, then we call that as translatory motion.
  • The translatory motion can occur along x-axis if I take if I take this, okay.
  • If the body moves only along X, that is translatory along X.
  • If the body moves only along Y, it is Y translatory motion.
  • The body can move along Z also.
  • Forward and backward with respect to the screen, okay.
  • Z axis, that is also translatory motion.
  • There could also be rotatory motion because of the application of the force.
  • What is this rotatory motion?
  • Because of which, and I take this as x axis, the thumb is x-axis, the forefinger is the y-axis, and the.
  • Middle finger is an axis.
  • If on application of the force, if this pen rotates, rotates about the x-axis, this is x axis, okay, this is x axis, if it rotates about the x axis like this, okay.
  • Then that is translatory motion along X.
  • Y axis, this is the Y axis, if the body rotates along the y-axis, then it is rotation along y.
  • Then you have z axis here, if the body rotates along the z axis, then it is rotation along the z axis.
  • Any translatory motion of this point because of application of the force can be represented along this three-coordinate system that is translatory motion along X, translatory motion along Y, and translatory motion along Z.
  • Best thing that we can do is or to understand this is you take a plane.
  • A plane which is moving.
  • If it is moving along X direction, then that is a transfer to motion along X.
  • Then if it rotates like this, this is rotation important.

Example or application from the lecture

  • For example, if I take the thumb as x-axis.
  • Now, if I take an object, say for example I take this pen, okay, this pen has got length and it has got diameter, so it's a three dimensional body.
  • The coordinate system that I can consider can be only 2D coordinate system.

Core explanation · 15:00–19:59

The x-axis, okay.

Key details

  • Then if the plane goes up and down, up and down, that is translatory motion along y.
  • If the plane rotates along the horizontal plane, if it rotates like this, if it rotates like this, then this is rotation along y.
  • Then if the plane moves perpendicular to the screen, to and fro, okay, that is transmittery motion along Z, and if it rotates like this, then it is rotation along Z axis.
  • I hope all of you have understood what are the different coordinate systems and what is translatory motion and rotatory motion.
  • Then if I take the x axis that is horizontal axis and the vertical axis as y, so the plane is perpendicular to our screen.
  • It can move along Y?
  • It cannot move along the Z because once we say it is moving along Z, then it is it is coming out of the plane.
  • Say I take this pen itself, which is in this plane, okay?
  • If it has to rotate about x, then it has to come out of the plane.
  • Can it rotate about the z axis?
  • No, this is the rotation along about z axis.
  • No, it is not possible, it is coming out of the plane, no.
  • But can it rotate about the z axis?
  • Two transfer motion, one along X and one along Y, if I am taking XY plane, and it can rotate about the Z axis.
  • It cannot rotate about the X axis, it cannot rotate about the Y axis.
  • Of course in addition to this mathematics, all of you should be knowing about addition, subtraction,.
  • Division and multiplication.
  • Along with this, you should also know what is dot product when it comes to vectors because all forces are vectors.
  • vector and cross product of vector.
  • These things have to be known by you before we start to understand engineering mechanics statics.
  • Close today's discussion.
  • This is class number two on engineering mechanics statics, which is a subject which is common to all students who are entering B Tech program in the first year.
  • I am Dr.
  • SV Venkatesh, a civil engineering.
  • from Department of Science and Humanities under PS University.
  • Hope to see you in the next class.
  • That is class number three.

Example or application from the lecture
